assumptions: The Jotform webhook payload contains a structured list of field answers that can be iterated over.
The Asana task will be created with a name derived from the form submission (e.g., first and last name) and all other answers placed in the description field.
No custom field mapping is required beyond the standard form fields; the integration will use the default description format for remaining fields.

sources.title: Webhook Payload Missing Quiz Fields in Wix
Webhooks: Detailed Documentation on Returned Data

notes: Jotform webhooks send data as a JSON string in the `rawRequest` parameter (multipart/form-data). The connector must parse `$_REQUEST['rawRequest']` (or equivalent) to access the submission payload.
The payload includes a top-level `id` (submission ID), `form_id`, `title`, and either a `flat` or `answers` object containing field values keyed by field name or ID.
Field names in the payload correspond to the form's field names (e.g., `first_name`, `email`) or auto-generated IDs (e.g., `q1_name`).
If using a bridge service (e.g., Zapier, Make), ensure it forwards the parsed JSON as `application/json` to the target.
The `workspace` field is required and must be a valid workspace GID.
The `name` field sets the task title; `description` sets the task notes.
No pagination applies to this endpoint as it creates a single resource.
